#!/bin/sh
# Nightly log backup. Bundles logs/ into a tarball and copies it to the destination.
#
# Destination is configured via the BACKUP_DEST environment variable, so the
# same script works whether backups land on local/mounted storage or on a
# remote host over ssh/scp. If BACKUP_DEST is not set, backups fall back to a
# local ./backups directory so the job never silently fails to produce output.
#
#   Local/mounted path:  BACKUP_DEST=/mnt/backups
#   Remote host:          BACKUP_DEST=user@backup-host:/srv/backups
set -eu

DEST="${BACKUP_DEST:-./backups}"
STAMP=$(date +%Y%m%d)
BUNDLE="logs-$STAMP.tar.gz"

tar -czf "$BUNDLE" logs/

case "$DEST" in
    *:*)
        # Remote destination, e.g. user@host:/path
        scp -q "$BUNDLE" "$DEST"
        ;;
    *)
        # Local path or mount point
        mkdir -p "$DEST"
        cp "$BUNDLE" "$DEST/"
        ;;
esac

echo "wrote $BUNDLE and copied it to $DEST"
